title: Perihelion account-specific lists, shared tags, and mixed folder access
content:
Perihelion moved another step toward a cleaner multi-account archive model. The direction is now more explicit: organization data belongs to the account that created it, existing archive organization stays attached to wm, and nothing is shared with other accounts unless the owner chooses to share it.

What changed:

  • Lists are now account-scoped: existing list records are normalized as wm-owned, and list visibility now respects ownership plus sharing rules.
  • Tags can be shared deliberately: tags remain account-owned, but a lightweight sharing metadata layer lets the owner mark a tag as private, shared with all accounts, or shared with selected accounts.
  • Options gained sharing controls: tags and lists now expose the same practical sharing choices: private, all accounts, or selected accounts.
  • Private is the default: regular accounts see their own tags/lists plus items explicitly shared with them; the owner keeps aggregate visibility and management control.
  • Folder access is easier to read: folder cards can now show a small Mixed indicator when child access rules contain both allow and block states.

This keeps Perihelion moving in the right direction: still a personal archive first, but now with a clearer account boundary, fewer accidental shared surfaces, and a better path for controlled collaboration. The work also fits the broader terminology cleanup across the platform, where owner and admin replace the older preferred/admin wording.

What worked: the existing JSON-based list structure could be extended without a disruptive migration, and tag sharing could be added with metadata instead of rebuilding the entire tag system. What still needs testing: the backend should be restarted, then verified with wm plus at least one regular account across private, all-account, and selected-account sharing.
